sections.title: Design Specification
sections.content:
**Overview**

Assembles and runs an interactive dspy.RLM-based Q&A agent that answers questions about a codebase using a codetwine project knowledge file.

- Another developer runs this file directly (`main()`) to start an interactive command-line loop that reads questions and prints answers about a project.
- A file wanting a ready-to-use Q&A agent calls `create_qa_agent(knowledge_path)` to get a configured `dspy.RLM` instance wired with tools, sandbox interpreter and instructions.
- A caller holding an RLM instance calls `ask(rlm, question)` to get a single answer string for one question.
- A caller needing just the summarized dependency graph (without full definitions/source/docs) calls `load_project(knowledge_path)` to build the `project_data` dict handed to the sandbox.
- A caller needing a Deno/Pyodide-backed sandbox for running LLM-generated Python calls `create_interpreter()` to get a properly configured `PythonInterpreter`.

This file depends on `knowledge_store.open_store` to open either a `project_knowledge.json` or `.sqlite` file behind the `knowledge_store.Store` abstraction, and on `qa_tools` (setting `qa_tools.store`, reading `project_name`/`dependencies()`, and registering `get_file_detail`, `search_text`, `read_source_file`, `get_files_using`, `graph_search` as RLM tools) to give the sandboxed LLM code access to file-level definitions, source code, dependency usages and design documents without loading them into `project_data`. No dependent information available (no other project file is shown importing from this one).

Design decisions worth knowing: `project_data` is deliberately shallow — only file paths, per-file summaries, callers and callees — so the sandbox never receives full source, definitions or design docs; those stay host-side and are fetched on demand through `qa_tools`. `project_data` and the knowledge `store` are held as module-level globals (`project_data` in this file, `qa_tools.store` in `qa_tools`) rather than passed explicitly, coupling `create_qa_agent`, `ask` and the tool functions to a single active session. The instructions text embeds a dynamically generated doc-section schema (via `build_doc_schema`) and the configured output language into a static template using plain string `.replace()`.

**Definitions**

## `LLM_MODEL`
Module-level constant naming the primary LLM (litellm-format string, e.g. `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"`) used to drive the `dspy.RLM` agent's reasoning; consumed in `create_qa_agent` when constructing the main `dspy.LM`.

## `SUB_LLM_MODEL`
Module-level constant naming the sub-LLM used inside the sandbox for `llm_query`/`llm_query_batched` calls issued by RLM-generated Python code; consumed in `create_qa_agent` to build `sub_lm`.

## `LLM_API_KEY`
API key read from the `LLM_API_KEY` environment variable at import time; passed to both `dspy.LM` instances (`lm` and `sub_lm`) in `create_qa_agent`. Empty string if the environment variable is unset.

## `LLM_API_BASE`
Optional override for a non-default LLM endpoint (e.g. Ollama, Azure); `None` by default, passed as `api_base` to both `dspy.LM` constructions.

## `OUTPUT_LANGUAGE`
Natural-language name (default `"English"`) substituted into `INSTRUCTIONS_TEMPLATE` at the `<<<RLM_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE>>>` placeholder so generated answers are produced in the desired language.

## `TARGET_KNOWLEDGE_PATH`
Default filesystem path to the knowledge file (`project_knowledge.json` under `sample_output/codetwine`), used by `main()` as the input to `create_qa_agent` when no other path is supplied; existence is checked before startup.

## `project_data`
Module-level dict, initially empty, populated by `load_project`/`create_qa_agent` with `project_name` and `project_dependencies`; read by `ask` on every call and passed as the `project_data` input field to the RLM signature.

## `INSTRUCTIONS_TEMPLATE`
Static multi-line string holding the RLM agent's system instructions, describing investigation rules, the `project_data` schema, the `get_file_detail` return schema and code examples for `search_text`, `graph_search`-style entry-point lookup, and doc-section reading; contains `<<<DOC_SCHEMA>>>` and `<<<RLM_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE>>>` placeholders filled in by `create_qa_agent` before building the `dspy.Signature`.

## `build_doc_schema`
Scans store entries via `iter_entries()` to find the first file whose `doc.sections` is non-empty, then renders that section list (`id`, `title`) as a markdown table describing the project's design-document structure; used to fill the `<<<DOC_SCHEMA>>>` placeholder so the agent knows which doc sections exist and can be searched.

## `load_project`
Opens the knowledge file through `knowledge_store.open_store`, assigns the resulting store to `qa_tools.store` (making it visible to all `qa_tools` functions), and builds the minimal `project_data` dict containing `project_name` and the full dependency graph from `store.dependencies()`; called once per session to prepare the data given to the RLM sandbox, and prints a load confirmation with file count and project name.

## `create_interpreter`
Locates the `PythonInterpreter`'s bundled `runner.js` and the local Deno cache directory (via `DENO_DIR` env var, `deno info --json`, or a default `~/.cache/deno` fallback), sets `DENO_DIR`, and constructs a `deno run` command with `--node-modules-dir=false` and `--allow-read` scoped to the runner script and Deno cache; used to work around Deno 2.x sandbox restrictions when instantiating `PythonInterpreter` for the RLM agent.

## `create_qa_agent`
Orchestrates full agent setup: calls `load_project` to populate the global `project_data` and `qa_tools.store`, constructs the primary and sub `dspy.LM` instances from `LLM_MODEL`/`SUB_LLM_MODEL`/`LLM_API_KEY`/`LLM_API_BASE`, builds the instructions string via `build_doc_schema` and template substitution, creates a `dspy.Signature("project_data, question -> answer", ...)`, builds the sandbox interpreter via `create_interpreter`, and assembles a `dspy.RLM` registering the five `qa_tools` functions as callable tools with `sub_lm` and the interpreter, then sets the primary `lm` on it; this is the main entry point for obtaining a ready-to-query agent.

## `ask`
Invokes the given `dspy.RLM` instance with the current global `project_data` and the supplied `question`, returning the `answer` field of the result; the thin call site used by both the interactive loop and any external caller wanting a single Q&A round trip.

## `main`
Validates that `TARGET_KNOWLEDGE_PATH` exists (exiting with an error message pointing to `main.py` if not), builds the agent via `create_qa_agent`, then runs an interactive REPL reading questions from stdin, printing answers via `ask`, and exiting on `exit`/`quit`/`q` or `Ctrl+C`; ensures the sandbox's Deno process is shut down via `rlm._interpreter.shutdown()` in a `finally` block regardless of how the loop ends.

summary: This file assembles and runs an interactive dspy.RLM Q&A agent that answers questions about a codebase using a codetwine knowledge file, wiring LLM config, sandbox interpreter, and qa_tools functions. Main definitions: create_qa_agent, ask, load_project, create_interpreter, build_doc_schema, main, project_data, INSTRUCTIONS_TEMPLATE, LLM_MODEL, SUB_LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY/BASE, OUTPUT_LANGUAGE, TARGET_KNOWLEDGE_PATH. Key terms: RLM agent, knowledge_store, qa_tools, PythonInterpreter/Deno sandbox, dependency graph, instructions template, interactive REPL, dspy.LM/Signature.
